text: Then I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven. He was wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow over his head; his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire.

versions.text: Then I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven. He was wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow over his head; his face was like the sun, and his legs like pillars of fire.
versions.explanation: πόδες means "feet," not "legs." The same word is rendered "foot" in verse 2 (πόδα), so "feet" here keeps the imagery and the vocabulary consistent across the two verses.

text: In his hand he held a little scroll, lying open. He set his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land,
and he cried out with a loud voice, like a lion roaring. And when he cried out, the seven thunders spoke with their own voices.
When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, but I heard a voice from heaven say, "Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down."
Then the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand to heaven

and swore by him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it: "There will be no more delay." [Footnote: Or "There will be no more time."]

versions.text: and swore by him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it: "There will be no more delay.
versions.explanation: χρόνος most literally means "time"; "delay" is an interpretive rendering. A brief footnote gives the reader the literal option without disturbing the oral flow.

text: "But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as he announced to his servants the prophets."

versions.text: But in the days when the seventh angel is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as he announced to his servants the prophets."
versions.explanation: The phrase τῆς φωνῆς ("of the voice/sound") has been dropped. Restoring it preserves the full Greek clause while still reading smoothly aloud.

versions.text: But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as he announced to his servants the prophets."
versions.explanation: The verse ends with a closing quotation mark, but no quotation is opened in this verse (the previous verse closes its own quote after "delay"). Adding an opening quotation mark balances the punctuation and signals to the reader that the angel's speech continues here.

text: Then the voice I had heard from heaven spoke to me again: "Go, take the open scroll from the hand of the angel who is standing on the sea and on the land."
So I went to the angel and asked him to give me the little scroll. He said to me, "Take it and eat it. It will turn your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."
I took the little scroll from the angel's hand and ate it. In my mouth it was sweet as honey, but when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.
Then I was told, "You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and languages and kings."
